question: What volatile matter (Vad) and fixed carbon (FCad) does the acid-washed sawdust (SD) used for co-pyrolysis with coal have?
rendered:
<document title="Effects of sodium on nitrogen evolution characteristics during the fast co-pyrolysis of coal and biomass">

=== page 1 ===
- Acid-washed and Na-loaded samples, including individual SD/LC and blended samples (blending ratios of 5% and 15%), were pyrolyzed in a vertical fixed-bed reactor at 500 °C and 800 °C. The evolution of volatile-N (measured as NH3 and HCN) and char-N functional groups was analyzed using an FTIR gas analyzer and employing X-ray photoelectron and Raman spectroscopies.
- Results show that at low temperatures of 500 °C, labile biomass N-A decomposes into NH3, while coal N-5 and N-6 remain relatively stable.
- At 800 °C, heterocyclic nitrogen undergoes ring-opening to form HCN, while coal preferentially retains nitrogen as N-Q.

Vad (volatile matter) = 77.45% for SD (acid-washed sawdust) at 500 °C, 
FCad (fixed carbon) = 14.65% for SD at 500 °C.
